candidate_readme:
# Agent Trace

Exports the agent loop as an OpenTelemetry trace: one span per run, turn, provider
request, tool execution and compaction, written to a local file in OTLP/JSON so a
collector or any OTLP-aware viewer can load it — while the session is still running.

```bash
pi -e ./examples/extensions/agent-trace/index.ts
```

The extension uses only the public extension API. It adds no dependencies, no tools and
no commands, and never fails a session: if the trace file cannot be written, tracing
stops, the agent is unaffected, and the failure is reported once (see below).

## The file

```
<SessionManager.getSessionDir()>/traces/<session id>.otlp.jsonl
```

The directory is created on demand. Setting `PI_AGENT_TRACE_FILE` replaces the path.

Every line is one OTLP/JSON `ExportTraceServiceRequest` holding exactly one span record:

```json
{"resourceSpans":[{"resource":{"attributes":[...]},"scopeSpans":[{"scope":{"name":"pi.agent-trace","version":"1"},"spans":[{...}]}]}]}
```

Resource attributes: `service.name` (`"pi"`), `service.version` (the coding-agent
package version), `pi.session.id`, `process.pid`.

Each span is written twice:

- a **start line** when the span starts — no `endTimeUnixNano`, no `status`, the
  attribute `pi.span.phase: "start"`, and the attributes that identify the span;
- an **end line** when it has ended — the same ids, name, kind and start time, every
  start-line attribute unchanged plus the rest, `endTimeUnixNano`, and `status`
  (`{"code":1}` = OK, `{"code":2,"message":...}` = ERROR).

A span with a start line and no end line is in progress (or was lost to a crash).
Nothing is ever rewritten or exported twice, so the file only grows: `/reload` and a
later pi process resuming the session continue the same trace, in the same file, under
the same trace id. A reader that tails the file and de-duplicates by span id (last line
wins) always holds the current state of the trace.

End lines appear in the order the spans ended, so `endTimeUnixNano` never decreases from
one end line to the next. An end line may lag its span's end by a moment: it is held
until pi has persisted the session entry the span names.

Loading a trace, for example with `jq`:

```bash
jq -c '.resourceSpans[0].scopeSpans[0].spans[0] | select(.endTimeUnixNano)' \
  ~/.pi/agent/sessions/<project>/traces/<session id>.otlp.jsonl
```

## Spans

| name | kind | parent | attributes on the end line |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pi.run` | INTERNAL | none (see sub-agents) | `pi.run.trigger`, `pi.run.turn_count`, `pi.session.entry_id`, `pi.run.after_compaction`, `pi.run.steer_count`, `pi.run.steer_entry_ids` |
| `pi.turn` | INTERNAL | the run | `pi.turn.index`, `pi.turn.stop_reason`, `pi.turn.tool_call_count` |
| `chat <model>` | CLIENT | the turn | `gen_ai.operation.name`, `gen_ai.system`, `gen_ai.request.model`, `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`, `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens`, `pi.usage.cache_read_tokens`, `pi.usage.cache_write_tokens`, `gen_ai.response.finish_reasons`, `pi.session.entry_id` |
| `execute_tool <tool>` | INTERNAL | the turn | `gen_ai.operation.name`, `gen_ai.tool.name`, `gen_ai.tool.call.id`, `pi.tool.is_error`, `pi.session.entry_id` |
| `pi.compaction` | INTERNAL | none (see sub-agents) | `pi.compaction.reason`, `pi.compaction.will_retry`, `pi.compaction.tokens_before`, `pi.compaction.first_kept_entry_id`, `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`, `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens`, `pi.session.entry_id` |

A run spans the agent loop, a turn its turn, a chat the assistant message, a tool its
execution, a compaction its preparation through to success or failure. Nesting is
strict; within a turn, tool spans start after the chat span ends, and concurrent tool
calls overlap as their executions did. Compactions happen between runs (or between two
turns of a run, when pi compacts before the next assistant response) and are root spans.
The summary requests a compaction makes are not chat spans.

`pi.run.trigger` is `prompt` for a run a user prompt started, `wakeup` for a run an
extension message started while pi was idle, and `continuation` for a run that follows
the previous one without settling in between — a queued follow-up, an automatic retry,
or an overflow retry. An overflow retry names no message of its own; it carries
`pi.run.after_compaction`, the entry id of the compaction that recovered it.

Messages the agent loop consumes while a run is already active (steering and follow-up
prompts, and extension messages delivered as `steer`/`followUp`) continue that run in a
new turn and are listed in `pi.run.steer_entry_ids`, in delivery order. A context-only
extension message is referenced by no span.

## Status

ERROR, with a message, for a tool result with `isError` (the result's text), an
assistant message that stopped with `error` or `aborted` and the turn containing it
(its `errorMessage`, else `aborted`), a failed compaction, and every span a shutdown
closed (`shutdown`). Everything else is OK — including a run whose turns failed.

## Session entries

Every `pi.session.entry_id` is an entry on the current branch, and the branch is covered
exactly once: user messages are named by their `prompt` or user `continuation` run, or by a run's
`pi.run.steer_entry_ids`; every assistant message (including aborted and failed ones),
tool result and compaction entry is named by exactly one span of its kind; an extension
message is named at most once. A span a shutdown closed may name no entry, because pi
had not persisted it yet.

## Sub-agents

Spawning tools opt into tracing through the public extension event bus. Inside
`execute(toolCallId, ...)`, obtain an environment for that specific call:

```ts
let env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv | undefined;
pi.events.emit("agent-trace:request-child-context", {
  callId: toolCallId,
  baseEnv: process.env,
  accept: (value: NodeJS.ProcessEnv | undefined) => { env = value; },
});
if (!env) throw new Error("No active trace context for this tool call");
const child = spawn(process.execPath, childArgs, { env });
```

The handler invokes `accept` synchronously and supplies a fresh copy containing
`PI_AGENT_TRACE_ID` and `PI_AGENT_TRACE_PARENT_SPAN_ID`. Unknown or ended calls
return `undefined`; without the tracer loaded there is no callback. Load this
extension in the child: every span joins the inherited trace, and every child
root (run and compaction) attaches to the named tool span. Children retain their
own default trace paths; choose a distinct child override if `PI_AGENT_TRACE_FILE`
is set. Do not replace the returned propagation variables before spawning.

The parent process environment is never modified, and each concurrent tool
requests its own call id. Nonparticipating tools still get normal tool spans;
automatic attribution from unmodified spawning tools is outside scope.

## Write failures

If the trace file cannot be written, tracing is disabled for the process — no exception
reaches pi, and tools and later turns run normally. The failure is reported once per
process as a custom message (`customType: "agent-trace"`) whose text starts with
`agent-trace: cannot write` followed by the path. It is delivered without starting a
turn and never enters the system prompt.
